snapshots.title: The push ended. The motion did not.
snapshots.alt: After Maz releases the cart, it keeps moving. The novel states that the push ended but the motion did not.
snapshots.body: The hand loses contact, so its force ends. The cart can still move. Real surface and air interactions can change its velocity.
snapshots.question: Which forces remain after release? How would an ideal zero-net-force case differ?
snapshots.work: Part 1 · Explain motion after the push

snapshots.title: One coin, two directions
snapshots.alt: Mr. Antocci explains that friction had little time to change the coin’s horizontal velocity. Mei explains that gravity made it fall after the card was removed.
snapshots.body: The supplied story shows little sideways motion and a downward fall. These are story observations, not measurements you collected.
snapshots.question: Which interaction changes each component of velocity? Does inertia supply another force?

snapshots.title: A passenger keeps moving
snapshots.alt: In a classroom toy model, the car stops while the passenger continues forward. Nadia says no new forward force threw it, and Mei explains that the strap supplies the force that slows it.
snapshots.body: Use the classroom frame. The car and passenger can change velocity at different times because different interactions act on them.
snapshots.question: Why does the passenger move forward relative to the car? Which interaction slows the passenger?

snapshots.title: No floor does not mean no force
snapshots.alt: Mr. Antocci says gravity still acts, especially the Sun’s. Mei says zero net force is a model, not the asteroid’s actual situation.
snapshots.body: Space lacks the classroom floor, but gravitational interactions remain. Constant velocity is a conditional model.
snapshots.question: What does zero net force predict? What evidence would challenge that model for the asteroid?
snapshots.work: Part 3 · Test the limits of the model
